title: Lior and the Thorn
premise: Mirabel Oyelaran, a memory-thief who trades stolen recollections on the smuggler roads of the Thornfell mountains, is forced to accept a dying courier's map—a chart of the living thorn-vine that has slowly consumed King Aldric's mind and now wears his crown. Hunted by the king's Thornsworn enforcers and betrayed by the fence who raised her, Mirabel must ally with Lior, a disgraced royal cartographer whose own memories she once stole, to reach the vine's heart beneath the palace. Along the way she learns the vine feeds on surrendered duty: it grows strongest where love is sacrificed for obligation. In the climax, Mirabel offers her most precious stolen memory—her mother's face—as a blade to sever the bond, and Lior must choose between restoring his stolen past and saving her. The king dies free, the vine withers, and Mirabel, finally belonging somewhere, chooses to stay rather than vanish.
about_author: Kestrel Vasquez is a former trail guide who spent six years leading expeditions through mountain passes that inspired the treacherous Thornfell. They write fantasy about people who survive by staying unseen, and live in a house full of maps they refuse to finish.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Faces
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. On a rain-slicked smuggler road, Mirabel lifts a merchant's first kiss from his mind and sells it to a grieving widow, establishing her trade and her rule: never be remembered. But a bloodied stranger collapses at her fire, pressing a wax-sealed map into her hands and whispering 'the crown is not the man' before dying. Emotional beat: unease—the invisibility she prizes has just been breached.

chapters.title: What the Map Refused to Show
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Studying the map in a safehouse, Mirabel finds it charts not roads but a body—the king's, threaded with living thorn. Thornsworn enforcers arrive hunting the courier's killer, forcing her to flee through passages only she knows. She realizes the map chose her because memory-thieves can touch what ordinary minds cannot. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into reluctant resolve.

chapters.title: A Cartographer Without His Country
chapters.summary: POV Lior. Disgraced royal mapmaker Lior Aldous recognizes the map's hand—it is his own missing work—and intercepts Mirabel on the high pass. He reveals he drew it while enslaved by the court, mapping the thing inside the king before escaping with his memory of how half-erased. Their uneasy bargain forms. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other's craft.

chapters.title: The Vine That Eats Devotion
chapters.summary: POV Lior. Sheltering in an abandoned shrine, Lior explains the thorn-vine's nature: it roots in acts of love surrendered to duty, and the king fed it for twenty years by burying everything he cherished. Mirabel tests this by stealing a memory from Lior and finding a woman's voice in it—proof his past was taken, not lost. Emotional beat: dawning intimacy laced with guilt.

chapters.title: Sablemarket
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. To forge court credentials they descend into Sablemarket, the black bazaar where Mirabel was raised by the fence Mother Quill—who promptly sells their location to the Thornsworn. Mirabel escapes the ambush but learns Quill has been trading her stolen memories for years; her own childhood is stock in another's vault. Emotional beat: betrayal cutting deeper than pursuit.

chapters.title: Thorns at the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Lior. Disguised as a surveyor's party, they enter the capital, where the vine's influence is visible everywhere—citizens smiling with thorn-shadowed eyes, duty worn like a leash. Lior is recognized by a former apprentice and must let Mirabel steal the boy's memory of him to save them both, watching himself be erased from a mind that loved him. Emotional beat: the cost of survival made intimate.

chapters.title: The Audience
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Brought before King Aldric, Mirabel touches his mind and meets the man still buried inside—flickering, begging, remembering a daughter he was made to renounce. The queen-regent, fully grown into the vine, orders Mirabel's execution, but the king's buried will stalls the guards long enough for escape through the palace's forgotten under-map. Emotional beat: compassion for the enemy.

chapters.title: Roots Below the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Lior. Following his own erased map-marks, they descend beneath the throne room to the vine's heart: a garden of white thorns fed by the king's sacrificed loves, each bloom holding a stolen memory. Lior finds his own past hanging there—including why he really fled the court. He cannot take it back without alerting the vine. Emotional beat: temptation at the point of no return.

chapters.title: The Severing
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. Confronting the queen-regent and the vine's flowering core, Mirabel understands the blade required: a memory given freely, not stolen. She offers her mother's face—the one thing she kept for herself—and drives it into the root. Lior, choosing her over his restored past, holds the wound open as the vine screams through every thorn-shadowed mind in the city. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into love.

chapters.title: What Remains When the Thorns Fall
chapters.summary: POV Mirabel. The king wakes diminished and human, weeping over a daughter's name he can finally say aloud; the city stirs free of its leash. Offered reward and restoration, Mirabel instead buys back nothing and burns her ledger of stolen goods. Lior asks where she'll go; she looks at the unfinished map between them and stays. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not stolen.
